audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] attributed the level 6 row to Sleepy Trouble Bubble 'adding real burst to her combo'.
audit.why: Sleepy Trouble Bubble is her E and is available from level 3 — it is not a level 6 spike. What actually arrives at 6 is Portal Jump: an 11/8/5s blink that lasts 1 second and then returns her to the origin point. That distinction is the whole reason Akali still wins the row.
audit.corrected: spikes[1] rewritten around Portal Jump and its snap-back.

audit.whatIsWrong: SLOT ERROR plus a missing mechanic. Zoe's blink was called 'Blink (W)' in seven places. And nothing anywhere said what the sleep actually does.
audit.why: Zoe's W is Spell Thief — she picks up the remnants of enemy summoner spells and item actives and casts them herself, gaining three homing missiles when she does. Her blink is Portal Jump, the R, on 11/8/5s. Calling it W sends the player looking at the wrong cooldown, and the advice built on it ('force Blink out early so she has nothing left to escape') is actively wrong: at 5 seconds maxed it is never meaningfully down. Separately, Sleepy Trouble Bubble reduces the target's Magic Resist while asleep AND the first source of damage that breaks the sleep is DOUBLED — that is the entire reason a landed bubble kills Akali, and it appeared nowhere on the page.
audit.corrected: Every 'Blink (W)' replaced with Portal Jump and its real cooldown; the MR shred and doubled wake-up damage now stated in breakdown.cooldowns, enemyWin and phases[3].why; Spell Thief added to wants.foe[3].

audit.whatIsWrong: The page told the player to bait out and track the blink, and gave no cooldown for anything.
audit.why: Portal Jump is 11s at rank 1 and 5s at rank 3 — you cannot build a plan on catching it down. Sleepy Trouble Bubble at 18/17/16/15/14s is the cooldown that actually gates her, and it is the one to count.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, wants.you[1] and content.mid now redirect the player from the blink to the 18-second bubble.

audit.whatIsWrong: The full layer refers to Zoe as 'he' and 'him' in tldr, winCon and report[0]/report[1], while the content layer correctly uses 'her'. enemyWin and breakdown.carry were also structural templates.
audit.why: The two layers render on the same page, so the reader sees the same champion described as both. The templates carried no Zoe-specific content.
audit.corrected: Pronouns fixed in all four full-layer fields; enemyWin and breakdown.carry regrounded on the bubble, the doubled wake-up and Portal Jump.

notes: Three defects. (1) SLOT ERROR: Zoe's blink was called 'Blink (W)' in seven places across both layers. Her W is Spell Thief; the blink is Portal Jump, her R. The advice built on the mistake was worse than the label — 'force Blink out early so she has nothing left to escape' is unworkable against an 11s cooldown that becomes 5s, and the page repeatedly told the player to catch her 'without Blink up'. All redirected to the 18-second Sleepy Trouble Bubble, which is the cooldown that actually gates her. (2) MISSING MECHANIC: nothing said what the sleep does. It reduces the target's Magic Resist and DOUBLES the first source of damage that breaks it — the reason a landed bubble kills Akali outright, and the substance behind the resistances-invalidated flag. Now stated in three fields. (3) PRONOUNS: the full layer called Zoe 'he'/'him' in four fields while the content layer used 'her', so the same page described one champion both ways. Fixed. Spell Thief was absent from the page entirely and is now in wants.foe[3]. FOR THE USER: this matchup's chart says Akali wins all seven rows and the tag says FAVOURED 4/10, but the win rate is 49.2% over 1624 games. All three sources (packet, full, content) agree with each other, so I did not override the chart — but it is the one place in my slice where the data and the rating pull in opposite directions, and it may deserve a second look. Unverified and therefore left alone: whether Twilight Shroud's untargetability prevents Sleepy Trouble Bubble from applying, whether Akali's own Q counts as the doubled wake-up hit when she breaks her own sleep, and whether Zoe can be hit by Akali's R while mid-Portal Jump.
